briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Transcript Drops, Tax Fight Turns Political: Momentum Builds on Both Fronts
briefs.top: The DEA just made the full 2,533-page rescheduling hearing transcript public, moving marijuana a step closer to a judge's recommendation on Schedule III/II status, while psychedelics notch fresh regulatory wins for psilocybin and MDMA therapy. In Michigan, the 24% wholesale tax fight is now a genuine campaign issue and a legislative target for repeal, even as C3 Industries keeps opening new stores and state cash keeps flowing to local governments.

local.text: Ann Arbor-based C3 Industries opened a new High Profile Cannabis dispensary in Luna Pier, right on the Michigan-Ohio border, betting on cross-border traffic from Toledo as part of its continued retail expansion strategy.

GOP gubernatorial nominee John James unveiled a cannabis platform pledging to repeal or sharply reduce the 24% wholesale tax if elected, arguing it 'drives up prices, gives illegal operators a competitive edge, and has already fallen far short of revenue projections' — putting real relief on the November ballot.

State Rep. James DeSana filed House Bill 6224, a one-line measure to repeal the wholesale tax outright, telling reporters 'it's time to repeal this failed tax and stop forcing taxpayers and businesses to pay for a policy that simply isn't working' — a bipartisan repeal push now has legs in Lansing.

Even amid the tax fight, the Cannabis Regulatory Agency is distributing nearly $100 million in marijuana tax revenue to more than 300 local governments and tribes, direct proof the industry keeps funding real community infrastructure and services.

Higher Love Cannabis Co. is consolidating to four Upper Peninsula stores, citing the wholesale tax's 'mounting tax burden,' but the chain says those remaining locations are 'the foundation for the company going forward' as it joins other operators pushing lawmakers for balanced policy fixes.

national.text: The DEA released the full, corrected 2,533-page transcript of its marijuana rescheduling hearing today, clearing the way for Chief Administrative Law Judge Derek Julius to draft his recommendation on moving cannabis to Schedule II or III — the next concrete step toward federal reform.

Compass Pathways landed an FDA rolling NDA review and a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher for COMP360 psilocybin in treatment-resistant depression, a designation that could shorten the review of COMP360 to one to two months after filing and puts the first potential FDA-approved psilocybin medicine on track for a first-half-2027 launch.

MDMA therapy for PTSD is back on the table: Resilient Pharmaceuticals (formerly Lykos/MAPS PBC) has resubmitted its NDA to the FDA without running a new Phase 3 trial, a notable comeback two years after the agency's rejection.

Trulieve Cannabis became the first plant-touching MSO to list on the NYSE (ticker TRLV), a milestone the company achieved via corporate restructuring following federal Schedule III reclassification — a signal that Wall Street's door is opening wider for cannabis operators.

Post-rescheduling deal flow is accelerating: acquisition fund Verdant is targeting single-state operators with at least $20 million in revenue and multiple locations, part of a wave of consolidation following the executive order directing cannabis to be reclassified as Schedule 3 — good news for strong regional brands looking for an exit or capital partner.
